dublinCore.title: Bathtub MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking
System Dynamics
Stock and Flow
Interactive Simulation
dublinCore.description: A p5.js MicroSim in which a source fills a bathtub, a drain empties it, and a chart plots the water height over time, so learners can see how the net flow changes a stock. A checkbox switches between a constant drain and a drain that follows Torricelli's law.

topic: Stock and flow: how inflow and outflow rates change a stock over time
learningObjectives: The learner will explain how the difference between the source flow rate and the drain flow rate changes the water height over time.
prerequisites: Reading a line chart of a quantity over time

misconceptions.misconception: The water height follows the source flow rate.
misconceptions.correction: The water height follows the net flow: the source flow rate minus the drain flow.

misconceptions.misconception: Turning the source down makes the water height fall.
misconceptions.correction: The water height keeps rising while the source is larger than the drain.

misconceptions.misconception: A tub drains at the same speed whatever its water height.
misconceptions.correction: Deeper water pushes more water through the drain.

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A bathtub stock and flow simulation. On the left, a bathtub holds blue water. A source pipe at the top left adds water and a drain pipe at the bottom right removes it. On the right, a line chart plots the water height over time. Start, Pause and Reset buttons control the simulation, and two sliders set the source flow rate and the drain flow rate. The water rises when the source is larger than the drain and falls when the drain is larger than the source. A checkbox makes the drain depend on the water height, so a fuller tub drains faster and the line on the chart becomes a curve.

userInterface.layoutPattern: simulation-left-chart-right, responsive width: the bathtub on the left and a linked time-series chart on the right, above a button row, two parameter sliders and a model-switching checkbox

controls.label: Start / Pause
controls.description: Run or pause the simulation (starts paused)

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Pause, return the tub to 75% full, clear the chart, restore both sliders and uncheck the checkbox

controls.label: Drain Flow Rate
controls.description: Constant drain: the drain flow on every frame. Torricelli drain: the drain flow of a full tub, and the label changes to Max Drain Flow Rate

controls.label: Drain depends on water height
controls.description: Unchecked: constant drain and straight chart lines. Checked: Torricelli drain, so a fuller tub drains faster, the chart lines curve and a Drain Flow readout appears under the tub

model.description: Discrete-time stock and flow with a constant drain or a Torricelli drain
equations: water height = water height + source flow rate - drain flow (each frame)
constant drain (checkbox unchecked): drain flow = drain flow rate
Torricelli drain (checkbox checked): drain flow = max drain flow rate * sqrt(water height / 200)
net flow = source flow rate - drain flow
Torricelli drain, source < max drain: settled water height = 200 * (source flow rate / max drain flow rate)^2
assumptions: Constant drain: the drain flow does not depend on the water height
Torricelli drain: the drain flow is proportional to the square root of the water height, and the slider sets the drain flow of a full tub
The tub has straight sides, so the water height is proportional to the volume of water
A full tub overflows, so the water height stops at 200
limitations: Units are pixels and frames, not liters and seconds
The Torricelli drain ignores viscosity, the vortex over the drain and the size of the drain opening, so it shows the shape of the curve, not the drain time of a real tub
The model advances one frame at a time (Euler's method), so the curve is a close approximation of the exact solution

variables.name: water height
variables.description: The stock: the height of the water in the tub

variables.name: source flow rate
variables.description: The inflow: water added to the tub on every frame

variables.name: drain flow rate
variables.description: Constant drain: the drain flow on every frame. Torricelli drain: the max drain flow rate, which is the drain flow of a full tub

variables.name: drain flow
variables.description: The outflow: water that leaves the tub through the drain on one frame

variables.name: net flow
variables.description: The source flow rate minus the drain flow. It is the slope of the line on the chart

assessmentQuestions.question: What settings keep the water height constant?
Why do a source of 1.0 with a drain of 0.4 and a source of 1.6 with a drain of 1.0 fill the tub at the same speed?
How would the chart change if the tub drained faster when it was fuller?
With the drain depending on the water height, why does the line get flatter as the tub empties?
With the drain depending on the water height, why does the tub settle at a level between empty and full?
Predict the chart line for a new pair of flow rates.
Explain in writing that the slope of the line equals the net flow.
Sketch the draining curve for a height-dependent drain, then compare it with the simulated curve.
